title: ‘Obsession’ Star Michael Johnston in Talks to Join ‘The Mummy 4’ With Brendan Fraser and Rachel Weisz
description:
“Obsession” star Michael Johnston is in early talks to join the fourth installment of “The Mummy,” Variety has confirmed.

	Johnston previously star
body:
“Obsession” star Michael Johnston is in early talks to join the fourth installment of “The Mummy,” Variety has confirmed.

	Johnston previously starred in the TV series “Teen Wolf,” but this year’s “Obsession” brought him to the attention of moviegoers when the low-budget Curry Barker horror film became a box-office sensation. 

	As previously reported, Academy Award winners Brendan Fraser and Rachel Weisz are officially returning for a fourth installment of the blockbuster franchise, “The Mummy.”
	

	Universal Pictures has dated the movie, directed by Radio Silence’s Matt Bettinelli-Olpin and Tyler Gillett, for a wide theatrical release on Oct. 15, 2027.


	Fraser and Weisz, whose involvement was first reported last fall, have closed deals to reprise their roles as adventurer Rick O’Connell and Egyptologist Evelyn O’Connell in the movie, plot details for which are being kept — not unironically — under wraps.

	Fan favorite John Hannah was also confirmed to return to the film’s franchise.

	“The Mummy” follows a treasure hunter who accidentally awakens a cursed Egyptian priest with supernatural powers. The movie and its 2001 sequel “The Mummy Returns” were major box office hits, reviving the classic monster movie IP and establishing Fraser as a bankable action star. Weisz, however, did not appear in the 2008 threequel “The Mummy: Tomb of the Dragon Emperor,” so her return to the franchise is particularly thrilling for fans.

	Bettinelli-Olpin and Gillett (“Ready or Not” and sequel “Ready or Not 2: Here I Come”) direct the new “Mummy” movie from a screenplay by David Coggeshall (“The Family Plan,” “Orphan: First Kill”). Sean Daniel — who has produced each installment of the $1.8 billion-grossing franchise at the studio since 1999’s “The Mummy,” including “The Mummy Returns,” “The Scorpion King,” “The Mummy: Tomb of the Dragon Emperor” and the 2017 Dark Universe project — also returns for the film.
	

	William Sherak, James Vanderbilt and Paul Neinstein, whose joint credits include “Nuremberg,” the Scream franchise and “The Night Agent” series, will produce through Project X Entertainment. 

	Clayton Townsend will produce.  Brendan Fraser and Hivemind’s Jason F. Brown will executive produce the film.

	Universal had no comment. 

	The news was first reported by The Insneider.

schema.headline: ‘Obsession’ Star Michael Johnston in Talks to Join ‘The Mummy 4’ With Brendan Fraser and Rachel Weisz

title: Zendaya Stuns ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Premiere in ‘Abstract’ Spider-Inspired Look: ‘It’s Like This Metamorphosis’
description: Zendaya stunned the red carpet at the “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” Los Angeles premiere in a black satin Ashi Studio corset with a sweeping architect
body:
Zendaya stunned the red carpet at the “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” Los Angeles premiere in a black satin Ashi Studio corset with a sweeping architectural train, putting an exclamation point on a press tour that the young star used as her personal runway.

	“It’s kind of an abstract way to present the spider,” Law Roach, Zendaya’s longtime stylist, told Variety of the look during the Monday night premiere. “You know, in our mind, it’s like this metamorphosis of this woman into this thing. And the jewelry is Boucheron.”
	

	While Roach said he “can’t pick a favorite” look from the tour, he shouted out the archival spiderweb dress from John Galliano’s 1997 “Circus” collection that Zendaya rocked in June at the London premiere of the Marvel sequel.

	When asked about his plans for the “Dune: Part Three” press tour, Roach was tight-lipped on details, but shared, “’Dune’ is a bit away, but it’s gonna be great. I’m excited.”

	Zendaya made headlines last month by skipping the couture and wearing a vintage Spider-Man T-shirt to a “Brand New Day” fan event in Paris. Roach scooped up the shirt on eBay for just $34.99. After the look when live, Roach posted the listing for the tee on his Instagram Story with the caption, “Style doesn’t always have to cost a fortune.”

	Zendaya stars alongside her husband, Tom Holland, in “Brand New Day,” which sees Peter Parker navigate a world in which his friends and family have forgotten him. Other cast members include Mark Ruffalo, Jon Bernthal, Jacob Batalon, Sadie Sink, Liza Colón-Zayas and Tramell Tillman. Destin Daniel Cretton serves as director.
	

	“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” hits theaters on July 31.

schema.headline: Zendaya Stuns ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Premiere in ‘Abstract’ Spider-Inspired Look: ‘It’s Like This Metamorphosis’

title: Ariana Grande Sues Hackers for Leaking Unreleased Music and Footage
description: Ariana Grande has filed a lawsuit against anonymous hackers, claiming that they gained backdoor access to devices that led to the leak of unreleased
body:
Ariana Grande has filed a lawsuit against anonymous hackers, claiming that they gained backdoor access to devices that led to the leak of unreleased songs and footage from recording sessions and music videos.

	The suit, filed on Monday in Los Angeles and reviewed by Variety, targets a group of unnamed John Does for phishing scams and hacking schemes that have caused “unlawful and egregious theft, dissemination, and exploitation of unreleased content.” Grande’s legal team outlines a pattern of illegal behavior in which hackers targeted the personal digital accounts of photographers and producers who worked closely with her and subsequently sold the data and content for “significant sums of money.”
	

	Grande is suing unnamed John Does to “uncover the identities of these currently unknown and unscrupulous individuals in order to hold them accountable for their invasive and reprehensible conduct.” The suit states that “it is imperative to Ms. Grande to ensure — on behalf of herself and others — that such conduct is deterred to the fullest extent possible.”


	The singer’s suit asserts that hundreds of leaks have occurred since she made her music debut in 2011. It claims that in 2019, hackers acquired the login for a Dropbox account that belonged to a photographer who had worked with Grande. The following year, the defendants hacked into the mobile device of a producer who had collaborated with Grande and accessed unreleased masters and demos and footage from recording sessions. In 2023 alone, hackers obtained access to 45 of her unreleased songs and leaked them.
	

	Additionally, the suit claims that in 2024, hackers created a Gmail account and domain name impersonating a photographer to get a digital technician to send unreleased photos that belonged to Grande.

	A representative for Grande did not immediately respond to Variety‘s request for additional comment.

title: ‘Bold Voice of Contemporary Horror’ Comic-Con Panelists Predict the Four Biggest Upcoming Trends in Genre Filmmaking
description:
Horror is red-hot at the box office, but what is up next for the genre?

	Ideas flowed freely at the San Diego Comic-Con panel for Bold Voice of Con
body:
Horror is red-hot at the box office, but what is up next for the genre?

	Ideas flowed freely at the San Diego Comic-Con panel for Bold Voice of Contemporary Horror: Tenth Anniversary Edition, which took place on July 24. Panelists included both actors and behind-the-camera talent, including Dan Stevens, star of AMC series “The Terror”; Deborah Ann Woll, star of Shudder’s upcoming thriller “The Cycle”; director Zachary Wigon, who helmed Bleecker Street’s “Victorian Psycho,” which debuted during this year’s Cannes Film Festival; and Dave Boyle, who directed SXSW audience award winner “Never After Dark.” The discussion was moderated by Michael Lerman, the co-founder and director of film programming at the genre-based Overlook Film Festival, and was curated by convention mainstay Rachel Walker, who founded the panel in 2015.
	

	What were their thoughts and theories? Read more below.

	
		Keeping audiences on their toes by not being boxed into one type of genre.	

	Touching on different tones is a great way to keep viewers discombobulated and primed for a scare.

	“I mentioned ‘The Descent’ as being one of my favorite movies. Part of the reason for that is that it shifts,” Woll said. “You’re not always quite sure what kind of horror movie you’re in. Is it a psychological thriller? Is it a survivalist thriller? Is it a creature feature? To me, films that can play with genre in that sense are often the most engaging. When I read this script [for ‘The Cycle’], that immediately made me say, ‘I have to do this.’”
	
		Bring in ideas from other types of storytelling, even if they’re not fully reflected in the final work.	

	Creatives should take from everything they’ve ever worked on — even if it doesn’t immediately seem transferable.
	

	“I think that the thing that really prepared me to jump into the genre was working on action, just because of how precise and communicative you have to be,” Boyle said. “There are so many moving pieces, so many things to think about and keep track of. Working in Japan for the first time, it’s interesting; Japanese scripts leave half the page blank. Then the director actually draws in the cuts where each cut is gonna happen, so that you have a real sense of how the movie’s going to come together, and there’s a real precision to it if you use that system and lean into it. That’s what prepared me to jump into my favorite genre, which is horror.”
	
		Horror mixed with humor continues to be on the rise.	

	This goes even beyond the influx of funny directors like Zach Cregger and Curry Barker making their mark on the industry.

	“Something I’m pleased to see spreading at the moment is horror with more humor attached,” Stevens said. “I find that humor is so powerful in horror and can often be overlooked. It’s sometimes a scary word when you mention that to producers: ‘I’d like to bring some humor into this.’ ‘It’s not a comedy.’ ‘I know it’s not a comedy, but by bringing some humor in, by bringing elements of humor, you bring in humanity, which I think exists in even the most batshit of situations.’ That can really ground a story sometimes. I’ve really enjoyed seeing a proliferation of those kinds of movies recently.”
	
		Revel in withholding some information from the audience to make for even bigger payoffs.	

	Conjure up interest by dropping some clues that don’t get solved right away.

	“I feel like horror is a subgenre of mystery,” Wigon said. “When I think about horror storytelling, it’s almost like you have a patchwork quilt, and you can’t see what’s in any of the patches at the beginning of the movie. Then as it goes along, you start to reveal that this is one little patch, that’s one little patch, and you’re creating mystery because the audience doesn’t understand how these patches connect to one another, and that’s the game that everybody’s playing. Then as it goes along, you start to realize that you’ve been looking at one image the whole film, and the pleasure is in seeing how these seemingly disparate pieces of information come to connect.”
	

	Watch the new trailer for “The Cycle,” which debuted during the panel, below.

schema.headline: ‘Bold Voice of Contemporary Horror’ Comic-Con Panelists Predict the Four Biggest Upcoming Trends in Genre Filmmaking

title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ First Reactions: Tom Holland Has ‘Never Been Better’ in a Sequel That Ditches ‘Multiverse Tedium’ and Delivers a ‘Grounded Spider-Man Tale’
description: “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” has finally been unveiled to members of the film press, who are calling Tom Holland‘s fourth standalone movie “a grounde
body:
“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” has finally been unveiled to members of the film press, who are calling Tom Holland‘s fourth standalone movie “a grounded Spider-Man tale” that is “thrilling, heartfelt and confidently character driven.”

	Fandango correspondent Erik Davis shared a glowing review on X, writing that director Destin Daniel Cretton’s sequel “feels deeper, more thoughtful and more mature than the previous trilogy.”


	“That maturity extends beyond the story to the action, with Cretton crafting some of my favorite Spider-Man fight sequences of the Holland era,” he added. “Part detective story, part psychological thriller, part buddy comedy (the Spider-Man/Punisher banter is so much fun), it stretches in exciting new directions before becoming a genuine love letter to the fans. When you see it, you’ll get it.”
	

	Critic Wendy Lee Szany wrote on X that she has “no notes” for “Brand New Day,” which delivered “top-tier action” and a few “tearjerker” moments. 

	TV host and entertainment journalist Brandon Pope echoed the praise. He wrote in his X review, “‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day‘ may be the most Marvel Marvel movie I’ve ever marveled. Destin Daniel Cretton honors beloved Spider-Man media – especially Raimi- to create something soulful + thrilling. Hulk, Punisher deliver. Big reveal lives up. The best of the Tom Holland Spidey series.”

	Film critic Peter Howell likewise adored the Marvel sequel. He wrote on X that “Brand New Day” cut back on the “multiverse tedium to give us a grounded Spider-Man tale that’s back to the city roots of the comic book hero we knew and loved.”
	

	“Tom Holland finally nails the sarcasm, angst and love hassles of Spidey/Peter Parker as Stan Lee first envisioned the character,” Howell added. “The film negotiates the emotional landmines left by ‘Spider-Man: No Way Home’ five years ago while a seriously scary villain emerges in the person of a malevolent telepath. Solid support from Zendaya, Jacob Batalon, Jon Bernthal, Mark Ruffalo and ‘Stranger Things’ star Sadie Sink.”

	Nexus Point staffer Kevin Verma wrote on X, “‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ is exactly the refresher Marvel needed. Tom Holland has never been better and the Spidey-Punisher pairing is pure gold. Destin Daniel Cretton outdoes himself, but the script is the real superhero- thrilling, heartfelt and confidently character driven.”

	Holland returns as Peter Parker/Spider-Man in “Brand New Day,” which is set four years after the events of “Spider-Man: No Way Home.” That movie ended with Doctor Strange casting a spell in which Peter is erased from everyone’s memory, so now the web-slinger is fighting crime in New York City without the support of MJ (Zendaya) and Ned (Jacob Batalon). A new threat emerges in the form of Sadie Sink’s mysterious villain at the same time as Peter’s spider powers begin evolving beyond his control. The supporting cast includes Mark Ruffalo as Hulk and Jon Bernthal as Punisher.

	Expectations for “Brand New Day” are sky high after 2021’s “No Way Home” became a pop culture sensation with $1.9 billion at the worldwide box office. It was Holland’s second billion-dollar-grossing “Spider-Man” movie after 2019’s “Far From Home” earned $1.1 billion on the heels of “Avengers: Endgame.” While Marvel has had its ups (“Deadpool and Wolverine”) and downs (“Captain America: Brave New World”) in recent years, “Brand New Day” should get the MCU back on strong box office footing ahead of December’s “Avengers: Doomsday.”

	Holland played a greater role in the development of “Brand New Day” compared to his previous “Spider-Man” movies. He took deep dives on the internet to understand what exactly Spider-Man fans wanted to see in his latest outing as Marvel’s iconic web-slinger, then took these fan ideas directly to studio executives and the movie’s screenwriters.

	 “What’s been really fun about this most recent movie is designing the suit and being a part of that process and understanding what we wanted to try and achieve,” Holland told LADbible about having greater involvement in the movie’s development this time around.
	

	“I have been actively sifting through the internet and trying to best understand what it is that the fans want from a ‘Spider-Man’ movie, and that’s been my driving force in these pitch meetings,” he added. “I think the producers, at times were like, absolutely sick of me, but I think it’s really important, because we make these movies for [the fans].”

	“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” opens in theaters nationwide July 31. Check out more first reactions in the posts below.

#SpiderManBrandNewDay reminded me why the story of Spider-Man resonates w/ me so much. He's hope. But he's also painfully human so bring tissues 😭Also the Tom/Zendaya chemistry was rom-com levels. And we need more Punisher in everything. And Sadie Sink… just wow! Liza too! pic.twitter.com/68jgm3htfs— Lyra Hale 🇵🇷🏳️‍🌈✍🏼 (@MsLyraHale) July 28, 2026




Peter Parker is changing, and so is the 'Spider-Man' franchise. #SpiderManBrandNewDay is the most emotional, most mature and most atmospheric installment in the franchise. It'll meet your expectations in some places and defy them in others. pic.twitter.com/iA0XsLl9rL— Brian Davids (@PickYourBrian) July 28, 2026


Spider-Man: Brand New Day is a solid new entry for Marvel. The story and themes of loneliness, change, and friendship all hit incredibly hard. It’s a bit overstuffed with too much going on at points. Sadie Sink’s story is the most weighty and shocking. #SpiderManBrandNewDay pic.twitter.com/QO6EKTkgXC— Hunter Bolding (@HunterBVideo) July 28, 2026


Destin Daniel Cretton brings incredible energy to the #Spiderman franchise. #Brandnewday is action-packed from start to finish. That sound design is incredible. this might be Tom Holland’s best outing as Spiderman to date. It’s the Summer of Tom Holland, Zendaya + John Bernthal— Jazz Tangcay (@jazzt) July 28, 2026

body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	Shark Week has officially returned, bringing another frenzy of great whites, makos and other underwater predators to Discovery Channel.

	The network’s annual programming event kicked off Sunday, July 26, and runs through Saturday, Aug. 1, with new specials airing nightly beginning at 8 p.m. ET. Cord-cutters can watch Shark Week live online through Sling TV, which carries Discovery Channel as part of its Sling Blue and Sling Orange + Blue packages.
	

	Sling Blue includes more than 40 live channels and allows subscribers to stream on as many as three devices simultaneously. The service also comes with 50 hours of cloud DVR storage, making it possible to record Shark Week specials and watch them later. 


	Viewers who miss the live broadcasts can also add Discovery+ through Sling. Discovery+ is available in an ad-supported plan for $5.99 per month or an ad-free plan for $9.99 per month, with Shark Week programming available to watch on demand.

	This year marks the 38th edition of Shark Week, with Discovery rolling out 20 new specials focused on shark behavior, attacks, conservation and ocean science. The lineup opened with “K-Pop Shark Heroes,” featuring comedian Ken Jeong and singer Rei Ami on a mission to challenge misconceptions about sharks across East Asia.

	Other highlights include “Air Jaws: Red, White and Breach,” which investigates great white sharks breaching along the U.S. coastline, and “Invasion of the Mega Sharks,” following researchers as they search for a potentially record-breaking great white off Nova Scotia.

	Later in the week, “Jurassic Sharks” uses CGI and real-world expeditions to examine prehistoric species, while “Jaws vs Orca” explores the growing evidence that killer whales are hunting great whites. “How to Train a Great White” tests whether the predators can learn and respond to cues, and “Ultimate Shark Dive” follows high diver Molly Carlson as she attempts a helicopter jump into a narrow shark cage.
	

	The week concludes Aug. 1 with “Great White Highway,” about the increasing number of great whites traveling along the East Coast, followed by “Thresher Shark: Stun to Kill,” which examines how thresher sharks use their powerful tails to incapacitate prey.

	Stream Shark Week on Sling TV.

title: ‘Dungeon Crawler Carl’s’ Breakout, Ryan Reynolds’ Jeanpool Stunt and More Comic-Con Highlights
description:
Jul 27, 2026 6:12pm PT	
	

	
		‘Dungeon Crawler Carl’s’ Breakout, Ryan Reynolds’ Jeanpool Stunt and More Comic-Con Highlights
body:
Jul 27, 2026 6:12pm PT	
	

	
		‘Dungeon Crawler Carl’s’ Breakout, Ryan Reynolds’ Jeanpool Stunt and More Comic-Con Highlights
	
	
			


			
			
	

									Getty
	

		
	
				
	A new fandom took over San Diego Comic-Con this year: “Dungeon Crawler Carl.”

	While there were plenty of Marvel and DC superheroes walking around the convention center and the surrounding Gaslamp Quarter (not to mention the Trekkies and “Star Wars” storm troopers, and the other comic book cosplayers), there were just as many people sporting t-shirts featuring Princess Donut, the tiara-wearing talking cat from the popular book series.
	

	In that sense, this year’s SDCC felt somewhat like a changing of the geek guard. Sure, hundreds of diehard Marvel fans began queuing for Saturday evening’s Hall H presentation on Thursday, but there was just as much buzz around newer (“Percy Jackson,” “The Vampire Lestat”)  and niche IP (“Neuromancer”), plus plenty of nostalgia fare (“Spaceballs,” “Grimm,” “Pan’s Labyrinth”).


	Here are some of the highlights:

	
		“Dungeon Crawler Carl’s” Warm Welcome	

	Author Matt Dinniman’s book series, which turns Earth into a video game-inspired alien game show, has skyrocketed in popularity — with more than 10 million copies sold — and just last month, Peacock ordered a live-action series produced by Seth MacFarlane. At Comic-Con, Dinniman hosted two panels alongside Jeff Hays, who voices more than 200 zany characters in the audiobook versions of the novels. To the delight of fans, Dinniman revealed that Hays will voice Princess Donut in the Peacock show. No other casting has been announced, but fans are patiently waiting to see how the beloved book series will come to life. Meanwhile, Dinniman is hard at work on the final two novels in the planned 10-book series.

	“There’s so much I want to tackle. All this stuff seems to be happening at once because we started doing it all at once,” he said, dropping by the Variety Studio, presented by Google TV. “I would love for there to be a full-on video game. … I would love to have an MMORPG, like a ‘Fallout’-style game, in the ‘Dungeon Crawler Carl’ universe. That’d be badass.”




	

					The “Avengers: Doomsday” cast — including Robert Downey Jr., Hayley Atwell, Lewis Pullman, Rebecca Romijn, James Marsden, Tenoch Huerta and Kelsey Grammer  — at the Marvel Studios Hall H presentation.
									Michael Buckner/Variety
	



	
		Marvel Readies for “Doomsday” and DC Bets on “Lanterns”	

	After skipping Comic-Con last year, Marvel fans were ready to see what’s in store for “Avengers: Doomsday,” which brings back Robert Downey Jr. as the new big bad, Doctor Doom. Marvel chief Kevin Feige packed Hall H with the movie’s A-listers — Pedro Pascal, Paul Rudd, Anthony Mackie and returning stars Chris Evans and Hayley Atwell were among those who made the trek — to show off an exclusive trailer that teased more of Doom’s backstory. But the breaking news was that Ryan Gosling will star in a Ghost Rider movie and Ryan Coogler’s “Black Panther 3” will introduce “Alien: Romulus” actor David Jonsson as the new hero, Prince T’Challa II, son of the late Chadwick Boseman’s T’Challa.

	DC Studios had a smaller presence at the con, focusing on previously announced projects instead of forecasting the future. The studio brought this summer’s “Lanterns” show, starring Kyle Chandler and Aaron Pierre, to Hall H. The HBO series, which puts a detective spin on the Green Lantern character, is expected to be a prestige hit for DC, and Pierre will reprise his Green Lantern role in next summer’s “Superman” sequel, “Man of Tomorrow.” In other movie news, “Clayface” star Tom Rhys Harries made a surprise appearance at the Jim Lee and Friends panel following the debut of a creepy new trailer for the horror thriller.




	

					Aaron Pierre, Kyle Chandler and Damon Lindelof during the “Lantern” Hall H panel. 
									Amy Sussman/Getty Images
	




	
		TV Titans	

	With summer movie season winding down, studios and streamers were eager to remind fans what’s coming to their televisions this fall. Apple TV came out swinging with a two-hour Hall H panel — the studio’s first major Comic-Con installation — that was largely dedicated to flexing its established hits like “Widows Bay” and “Silo,” plus a first look at the highly anticipated sci-fi drama “Neuromancer,” with Callum Turner, and “Matchbox the Movie,” starring John Cena and Jessica Biel. Prime Video focused on heavy-hitting IP vehicles in “The Lord of the Rings: Rings of Power,” “Blade Runner 2099” and “Carrie” from Mike Flanagan. “Rings of Power” has tons of momentum heading into Season 3 with the addition of geek-god Jamie Campbell Bower (who played Vecna on “Stranger Things” and showed off his DJ skills at IGN’s party), while “Blade Runner 2099” seems destined for hit status thanks to the star power of co-leads Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer, and a confident vision from showrunner Silka Luisa.




	

					Jamie Campbell Bower performs at Prime presents the IGN San Diego Comic-Con Party 2026 at Hard Rock Hotel San Diego.
									Getty Images for Prime
	





	
		Indie Spirit	

	SDCC isn’t just for comic book lovers; there’s plenty to keep cinephiles entertained, too. Over the past few years, indie distributors Neon and A24 have used the convention as a launching pad for some of their buzziest titles — especially horror movies, like “Together” and “Talk to Me.” This year, SDCC scheduled back-to-back showcases for a couple bloody-good films: Na Hong-jin’s “Hope” from Neon and Adam Wingard’s “Onslaught” for A24. For his first trip to Comic-Con, director Na detailed the 10-year journey to make his alien invasion action movie — and made the crowd cackle by revealing that “90%” of the characters don’t make it to the end credits.

	The “Onslaught” crew — SDCC-vets Wingard, Adria Arjona, Dan Stevens and Rebecca Hall, with fan favorite Drew Starkey (welcomed by ear-piercing shrieks from the audience) — debuted a new trailer for the blood-soaked action movie. Arjona stars as a badass Army sniper grappling with PTSD, who must protect her young daughter from a rogue squad of genetically engineered super soldiers.

	“I just felt crazy protective over her,” Arjona said of her young co-star, Blake Kennedy. “It’s that beautiful mother feral need to make sure that your child is fine.”




	

					Drew Starkey, Rebecca Hall, Dan Stevens, Adria Arjona, Adam Wingard and Kevin Smith at A24’s “Onslaught” panel at San Diego Comic-Con.
									Michael Buckner/Variety
	




	
		Cosplay Cameos	

	Cosplay isn’t only for the fans; superstars went incognito to create some of the convention’s best surprises. (Think Andrew Garfield walking up to the mic in full Spider-Man costume 15 years ago.)

	This year, Rick Moranis made his Comic-Con debut to promote the long-awaited “Spaceballs” sequel, “The New One,” which ends his 30-year acting hiatus. The Hall H crowd went berserk when Moranis revealed himself from under a gigantic Lord Dark Helmet helmet.

	Johnny Depp transformed into the “Christmas Carol” curmudgeon Scrooge for his surprise appearance at an activation for “Ebenezer.” A crowd of hundreds braved the San Diego heat for a couple of hours in hopes of catching a glimpse of the actor. “Have you no jobs?” Depp (as Scrooge) croaked, ribbing the crowd before heading to Hall H to debut the movie’s trailer.

	But the grand prize goes to Ryan Reynolds, who crashed Marvel Studios’ Hall H presentation dressed as “Jeanpool” — a Canadian tuxedoed Deadpool, which might also be a subtle nod to X-Men’s Jean Grey — to beg for a role in the new “Avengers: Doomsday.” After the convention, Reynolds revealed that he traipsed around the convention floor without handlers or security, shaking hands and taking selfies with fans — all without getting recognized.



	

					Rick Moranis speaks during the “Spaceballs” Hall H panel.
									Amy Sussman/Getty Images

ABC has announced a slate of fall premiere dates.

	After some football kickoffs, “Dancing With the Stars” will return with a two-episode premiere on Sept. 15. Celebrity cast members include Ciara Miller, Maura Higgins and Jackson Olson, with more to be announced.

	“America’s Funniest Home Videos” will also have a two-episode premiere on Sept. 27, followed by the Oct. 30 premieres of “Scrubs” (its second season of the reboot and 11th overall) and “Shark Tank,” which returns with Barbara Corcoran, Robert Herjavec, Lori Greiner, Daymond John, Daniel Lubetzky, Kevin O’Leary, Kendra Scott and Rashaun Williams. Guest sharks include MrBeast, Mindy Kaling, J.J. Watt, Steven Bartlett and more.

title: Sean Astin Says ‘I Had to Sell My House’ During ‘Lord of the Rings’ Era Because $250,000 Payday Was So Low: ‘I Negotiated Such a Small Amount on the Trilogy’
description: Sean Astin said in a new interview with The Guardian that he was forced to sell his house amid “The Lord of the Rings” fame in the early 2000s becau
body:
Sean Astin said in a new interview with The Guardian that he was forced to sell his house amid “The Lord of the Rings” fame in the early 2000s because he negotiated such a small salary to play Samwise Gamgee in Peter Jackson’s landmark movie trilogy. The reveal may come as a shock to fans considering the “Rings” movies were cultural phenomenons that grossed $2.9 billion at the worldwide box office between 2001 and 2003. 

	“I was not prepared for that level of visibility and access,” Astin told the publication. “And there was a disconnect between the attention that I was getting and how much money we had. It was not a lot of money! In fact, I had to sell my house because I negotiated such a small amount on the trilogy.” 
	

	Astin noted that he is “very comfortable financially now,” but that wasn’t the case when “The Lord of the Rings” was dominating box office charts. Peter Jackson and the team behind the “Rings” trilogy famously shot all three movies at once, meaning there was no opportunity for the cast to renegotiate their salaries based of the success of each installment. 

	“Because we weren’t making one movie and then renegotiating a contract for the next, it wasn’t the sort of lucrative scenario that you could sort of rest easy for the rest of your life,” Astin’s “Rings” co-star Elijah Wood told Business Insider last year. Wood noted that New Line Cinema took a “real gamble” filming all three movies at once. To mitigate financial risk, the ensemble cast was offered “not massive salaries,” the Frodo actor said. 

	“The benefit of that was that we were also signing up for something that was going to be a part of our lives forever,” Wood added at the time.
	

	Astin previously revealed that he earned around “$75,000 a movie,” brining his total “Rings” salary to around $250,000. Co-star Orlando Bloom (who played Legolas) said in a 2019 interview on “The Howard Stern Show” that he was paid just $175,000 for the trilogy.

	“The Lord of the Rings” franchise is currently developing its big screen return courtesy of “The Hunt for Gollum,” which Andy Serkis is currently directing, and a new movie co-written by Stephen Colbert. Astin is not confirmed yet to reprise his role in either project, but he will certainly fight for better pay if he is, telling The Guardian: “Goddamn right.”

title: D4vd Ordered to Stand Trial for Murder of 14-Year-Old Girl
description:
A judge ruled that singer D4vd must stand trial for allegedly killing and dismembering a 14-year-old girl.

	On Monday, Los Angeles Judge Charlaine
body:
A judge ruled that singer D4vd must stand trial for allegedly killing and dismembering a 14-year-old girl.

	On Monday, Los Angeles Judge Charlaine Olmedo determined during a preliminary hearing that there is enough evidence for the case to go to trial. “The people have met their burden on all counts,” said Olmedo during the conclusion of the hearing, reports AP. D4vd, whose real name is David Burke, will continue to be held without bail.
	

	The preliminary hearing began last Tuesday with prosecutors showing grisly photos taken from the crime scene where the body of the victim, Celeste Rivas Hernandez, was found in September 2025. The pictures showed her dismembered body parts in the front trunk of Burke’s Tesla. Prosecutors claimed that Burke had purchased two cadaver bags, a shovel and three different chainsaws following Hernandez’s murder.


	Throughout the week, prosecutors laid out various allegations and findings. They claimed that nearly a dozen air fresheners were found in the Tesla where Hernandez’s body was discovered, and an LAPD Criminalist stated that blood found inside Burke’s garage was consistent with Rivas’ DNA, according to People. Prosecutors also alleged that Hernandez and Burke texted about terminating a pregnancy when she was 14 years old, and messages shown in court on Monday suggested that Hernandez threatened to destroy Burke’s career before her death. After prosecution rested, Burke’s defense team chose not to call any witnesses.

	Burke was arrested this past April and charged days later with a first-degree murder charge that could make him potentially eligible for the death penalty. He is also set to face charges for lewd acts with a child and for dismembering her body. Burke pleaded not guilty to the charges.
	

	Hernandez was last seen alive on April 23, 2025, when she went to Burke’s home in the Hollywood Hills. In September 2025, her body was found in multiple bags in the front trunk of Burke’s Tesla. Her arms and legs had been cut off and her body had significantly decomposed.

	The Los Angeles County medical examiner released an autopsy report showing that Hernandez died of multiple stab wounds and that the manner was “homicide.” She died from “multiple penetrating injuries.”

	In April, prosecutors alleged that D4vd had a “significant amount” of child pornography on his iCloud storage account during a hearing. Beth Silverman, deputy district attorney for Los Angeles County, said they uncovered eight terabytes of data on an iCloud account but had only been able to download one terabyte thus far. They also had found 20 to 30 terabytes of raw data across various devices. Burke had appeared at the hearing in an orange jumpsuit and was “slumped” in his chair.

            Michelle Hadley spent 88 days in jail for a twisted stalking plot she had nothing to do with ... and now we know how much money was shelled out to her over the massive screw-up.
      
    
            Here's the deal ... Michelle is the focus of a new Netflix documentary, "A Toxic Love Story," about a 2016 cyberstalking case out of Anaheim ... where she was tossed into the clink after her ex-boyfriend, Ian Diaz, and his fiancée, Angela Connell, framed her for outlandish crimes ... such as trying to arrange for Angela to get raped via a Craigslist ad.
      
    
            Sources with direct knowledge tell TMZ … Michelle settled with Anaheim police for $1.8 million back in 2021 ... after she sued the city for what the doc shows was sloppy, rushed police work -- all because Ian used his influence as a U.S. Marshal at the time.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            We're told her attorneys received 40% of the settlement ... and she didn't have to pay their taxes because it was a civil rights case.
      
    
            Still, we're told Michelle's portion was taxed ... and her family also dropped about $35,000 on attorneys' fees during her criminal ordeal.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The Netflix doc say she settled her lawsuit with the police ... but the amount was not shared, so TMZ looked into it.
      
    
            At the end of the day, Michelle ended up with about $800K ... which she spent on a new condo in Connecticut and finishing her master's degree in marketing at Chapman University.

                                  July 27, 2026
                                4:25 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Ariana Grande is going after people she says hacked into the digital accounts of photographers and producers she worked with ... stealing and leaking unreleased music, private photos and videos.
      
    
            The pop superstar filed a lawsuit in California Monday against several unnamed individuals, hoping the legal action will uncover who is behind the alleged breaches.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            According to the complaint, obtained by TMZ, Ariana says this was not an isolated incident ... claiming she has repeatedly been targeted by cyberattacks throughout her career, including recently.
      

            She claims the stolen material included unreleased songs, photos and video and audio recordings tied to her creative process -- none of which was intended for public consumption.
      
    
            The alleged hackers then sold her personal data and content on the dark web for "significant sums of money," Ariana claims ... causing her "substantial and irreparable harm."
      
    
            The suit targets up to 100 John Does ... including the alleged hackers, people and businesses accused of helping distribute the stolen material, and even those allegedly shopping it to potential buyers or purchasing it.
      
    
            Ariana is asking a judge to stop the alleged theft and distribution ... while also sending a warning to would-be hackers.
      
    
            She says artists deserve to control when and how their work is released -- and stealing and leaking it violates both their privacy and their creative rights.
      
    
            Story developing ...
